svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 44: the dovecote in the fort's second upper storey
svg.text: Entry 44 (IX 17–X 2) — the dovecote in the fort's second upper storey
Schematic section (side view), with a plan inset, north up. One arrangement the text allows; not a reconstruction of any real site.
Main reading (text shown): the dovecote in the second upper storey, entered from above
Section through a fort of three levels. The dovecote · שובך is in the second upper
storey · עליאה השנית; its way down · ירידתו comes from above · מלמעלא. No sizes are given.
fortress of Nab · מצד נאב, drawn as a tower-like block
Side view; the text gives no orientation for the section.
Plan: in the district of the south
Neither the district nor the fort is located.
Milik 1962: the second ascent, not storey
in DJD III: the place is reached by a second climb.
the dovecote stands at the top
Milik: שובך as an opening, not a dovecote
As at entry 38, Milik reads an opening or inspection hole;
most editors, Puech among them, read a dovecote.
Alternative sense · not the text shown
no pigeon niches: the deposit is
in an opening of the second upper
Only Milik 1960 would change the plan, and it is not adopted.
Names move the place · Milik 1960 rated weak or ruled out
• Text shown: “fortress of Nab”, letters divided as מצד נאב.
• Puech 2015: one word, “in the small fort”; Puech 2006: Maṣad-na.
• Milik 1960: aque[duct] of ha-Masad, Masada; depends on an emendation
“In the dovecote that is in the fortress of Nab, in the district of the south, in the second upper
storey, its way down from above: 9 talents.”
The letters as divided in the text shown, “fortress of Nab”; Puech 2015 asks only for a fort of at
least two levels. The upper storeys are counted above the ground storey, which the text does not say.
“Its way down from above” is drawn as a hatch and ladder through the roof. No position inside the
fort, and no depth, is given.
Possible only, low. Tekoa–Herodium sector (Puech's area for IX 4–X 4): an area of about 8 km, no site
SWP reports a fortress, a large reservoir and an aqueduct at Herodium, which it ties to Herod;
dovecotes are attested for the district only in texts, Milik C4 (phase5_assessments.csv, DN 39-45).
The lexicon rates dovecote medium-high, fort medium and upper storey medium.
